name: Peyton Mercer

biography.name: Peyton Mercer

background.family: Lives with two fathers and an older brother; home life is predictable, affectionate, and occasionally over-scheduled.
background.finances: Comfortable middle income, with a household budget that prioritizes local activities over expensive travel.
background.geography: Plano, Texas, near parks and a recreation center.
background.cultureLanguages: English-speaking family with Canadian and Texan relatives; she was adopted as an infant and decides for herself when that is relevant to conversation.
background.school: Large public high school with statistics, art, and sports programs.
background.accessOpportunities: Collin College workshops, municipal recreation classes, and university outreach in Dallas are accessible through family rides.

timeline.story: Peyton liked balancing on curb edges and sorting picture cards into categories that changed daily. Her fathers learned to ask for the rule rather than assuming she had made a mistake.
She started swimming and loved seeing her lap times improve. She also spent long stretches drawing pretend menus, carefully pricing foods she had never tasted.

A skateboard borrowed from a neighbor became a shared weekend project. Falls frustrated her, but she liked repeating a movement until it changed. A school science fair felt less satisfying because she had chosen a topic mainly to impress the teacher.

She helped look after a baby cousin and found reading the child's changing signals unexpectedly absorbing. At school she enjoyed collecting survey responses but became bored writing the required introduction.

Peyton quit competitive swimming after the early schedule crowded out friends. She kept swimming recreationally and began using simple spreadsheets to compare skateboarding practice sessions, although her tiny samples rarely supported the conclusions she announced.

An art teacher encouraged her to draw moving people instead of perfect objects. She enjoyed the uncertainty. A statistics unit made her revisit old practice charts and notice that sleep and weather complicated the story she had told about improvement.

She skates with friends, babysits a familiar cousin, and helps a teacher organize anonymous class survey results. She likes numbers when they concern real people or movement, but remains unsure whether she enjoys mathematics itself or the questions it helps answer.
